Only the review bundle classifier consumes the lists; review-bundle-convergence and review-subject-capabilities integration passed.
No logging change; an unclassified path is still reported by name in the seal refusal.

Classification only widens: paths that were refused as unclassified now seal; no previously classified path changed class. install-and-upgrade-journeys and review-subject-capabilities integration passed in the sealed run.

Independent probe beyond the scan: every filepath.Join on a pose-dir variable (poseDir and similar) names only schema-version and transfers, both classified; so the literal-pattern blind spot holds no unclassified name today. The .pose/LICENSE and .pose/NOTICE classification (documentation, included) matches the generic rule for license and notice basenames. Minor, non-blocking: the install test discards the WalkDir error, so a missing .pose would pass vacuously; freshInstall always creates it.

Reviewed the four commits with POSE-Spec: pose-review-subject-classifies-engine-records (edc003e2, 47d8a834, 9b957f43, 32a1a449): artifact-check --strict gives 7 claims equal 7 observed; nothing outside review_bundle.go, the two tests and the spec records.

Extending two hand-kept lists plus a source-scan guard and an install/update guard is the smallest change; no classifier redesign.
